official.deadline_note: No single ADB deadline: applications must be sent to the chosen academic institution at least six (6) months before the planned commencement of studies.
official.application_cycle: Ongoing, institution-led intake (apply at least six months before the intended start of studies)
official.status_note: The programme operates continuously; ADB instructs applicants to send applications to a designated institution at least six months prior to the planned time they wish to commence studies.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The ADB-Japan Scholarship Program provides full tuition fees.
benefits: For scholars engaged in research, a special grant may be available for thesis preparation; in special circumstances, computer literacy, preparatory language and other similar courses may be covered
eligibility: National of an ADB borrowing member country and Japanese ODA scholarship-eligible country
Not hold dual citizenship of any developed country
Gained admission to an approved master's course at a Designated Institution
Hold a bachelor's degree or its equivalent with superior academic record
At least two (2) years of full-time professional working experience acquired after a university degree, with proficiency in oral and written English communication skills
Not be more than 35 years old at the time of application, unless waived in exceptional cases with the expressed endorsement of the Government of Japan
Agree to return and work in your home country for at least two (2) years after completion of studies

Not be an Executive Director, Alternate Director, management, staff or consultant of ADB, or their close relatives; not be staff of an ADB-JSP Designated Institution; not be living or working in a country other than your home country; not be already enrolled in graduate degree programs
requirements: Request information and application forms from your chosen academic institution
Indicate to the academic institution that you are applying for admission and would like to be considered for the ADB-JSP Scholarship
Submit the completed institution application form and required documentation, including the ADB-Japan Scholarship Program information sheet
Submit your latest income tax return or certification of annual/monthly salary, whichever is available, and a certification of family income (parent's income)
Send the application at least six months prior to the planned time you wish to commence studies
documents: ADB-Japan Scholarship Program information sheet (application sheet form)
Latest income tax return or certification of annual/monthly salary
selection_criteria: The academic institution screens and ranks applicants based on its own selection criteria, keeping in view the eligibility requirements and selection criteria of ADB
ADB reviews the institutional submissions and recommends awardees based on its selection criteria to the Executive Director of Japan for formal approval
coverage: Special grant may be available for thesis preparation for scholars engaged in research
application_method: Request information and application forms from your chosen academic institution
Complete the institution application form and the ADB-JSP application sheet
Submit the complete documentation to the academic institution at least six months before your intended start of studies
The institution screens and ranks applicants and submits its ranked list to ADB; ADB recommends awardees to the Executive Director of Japan for formal approval
official.application_route: No separate application to ADB: apply for admission to a designated institution and indicate you wish to be considered for the ADB-JSP, submitting documents at least six months before your intake
official.citizenship_residency: Available to citizens of the published ADB borrowing member countries that are Japanese ODA scholarship-eligible (Afghanistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Georgia, India, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kiribati, Kyrgyz Republic, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Maldives, Marshall Islands, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nauru, Nepal, Niue, Pakistan, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Turkmenistan, Tuvalu, Uzbekistan, Vanuatu, Viet Nam); no developed-country dual citizenship, and applicants must not be living or working outside their home country
official.international_eligibility: For nationals of the published eligible countries to study at 27 designated institutions across Asia and the Pacific, including 17 in Japan
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Graduate study in economics, business and management, science and technology, and other development-related fields at one of the 27 designated institutions
official.description: Since April 1988, with financing from the Government of Japan, ADB has offered citizens from developing member countries the opportunity to pursue graduate studies at 27 selected educational institutions across Asia and the Pacific, including 17 in Japan, so that scholars return to their home country afterwards to apply and share their new knowledge and skills to promote socioeconomic development.
official.program_type: Multilateral scholarship financed by the Government of Japan and administered by the Asian Development Bank
official.english_requirement: Applicants must have proficiency in oral and written English communication skills to be able to pursue studies (no score published)

verification.notes: Verified on ADB's official programme and procedures pages: about 130 graduate scholarships a year (the main programme page; the procedures page states about 135), full tuition fees, monthly subsistence allowance including housing, books, medical insurance and travel expenses, the published eligibility list, and the institution-led application route at least six months before start; no monetary value is published.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply to ADB directly: you apply for admission to one of the 27 designated institutions, tell that institution you want ADB-JSP consideration, and submit at least six months before you intend to start. Check the hard barriers before investing time: you need at least two years of full-time professional experience after your bachelor's degree, you must be 35 or under, and you must commit to returning home for at least two years after graduating. Note what the award excludes: family expenses, extra-curricular courses or training, additional travel, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships and computers are not covered, and admission by itself is not a scholarship award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career professionals under 35 from ADB borrowing/ODA-eligible countries with a strong bachelor's record, two years of work experience and a development-focused master's at a designated institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your nationality against ADB's published eligible-country list and confirm no developed-country dual citizenship
Confirm you meet the 35-year age limit and have two years of full-time post-degree professional experience
Choose a designated institution and programme, then request its application forms
Prepare income documents: latest income tax return or salary certification, plus certification of parents' income
Submit the institution application plus the ADB-JSP application sheet at least six months before your intended start
Do not resign from your job until the institution confirms you have been awarded the scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to ADB instead of through an academic institution
Missing the six-month lead time before the intake
Lacking the required two years of full-time professional working experience
Being over 35 without an exceptional Government of Japan endorsement
Incomplete or inaccurate documentation, which ADB warns can void an award even after selection
Assuming admission by the institution equals a scholarship award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Expenses for the scholar's family; extra-curricular courses or training; additional travel during the study program; supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships; and purchase of educational equipment such as computers
document_audit: Both the institution's own application and the ADB-JSP information sheet must reach the institution
Income certification is mandatory: latest tax return or salary certification plus parents' income certification
The institution must formally endorse and rank you before ADB will consider your application
alerts: There is no ADB deadline; your real deadline is the institution's, at least six months before intake
Only about 130 awards exist across 27 institutions, so institutional ranking is the effective competition
The two-year return-home service obligation is a condition of the award
ADB's main page states about 130 scholarships a year while its procedures page states about 135
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the designated institution with the ADB-JSP application sheet; the institution screens and ranks and sends its list to ADB; ADB recommends awardees to the Executive Director of Japan for formal approval; the institution then informs all applicants of the outcome.
